journeys.name: Abraham's journey
journeys.blurb: From Ur of the Chaldees to the oaks of Mambre — a lifetime spent walking toward a promise.

stops.t: Terah takes his family out of Ur of the Chaldees.
Terah dies; God calls Abram, aged 75: 'Go forth out of thy country'.
First stop in Canaan. The Lord appears: 'To thy seed will I give this land'. Abram builds an altar.
A second altar between Bethel and Hai; Abram calls on the name of the Lord.
Famine drives him to Egypt, where he passes Sarai off as his sister.
Back at the altar. Abram and Lot part; Lot chooses the Jordan plain.
He settles by the oaks of Mambre. The covenant, the three visitors, Isaac's birth.
A well and a treaty with Abimelech; Abraham plants a grove and calls on the everlasting God.
Three days' journey to the mountain where Isaac is bound and spared.
Sara dies; Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah — the first piece of the promised land he owns.

journeys.name: The Exodus
journeys.blurb: Out of Egypt, through the sea, to the mountain — and forty years to the Jordan.

stops.t: The night of the Passover; six hundred thousand set out in haste.
First camp. Unleavened bread; the pillar of cloud and fire appears.
Trapped between Pharaoh's chariots and the water. 'The Lord will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace.'
Bitter water made sweet by a tree.
Quails in the evening, manna in the morning.
Water from the rock; Amalec defeated while Moses' arms are held up.
The Ten Words, the covenant in blood, the golden calf, the tabernacle. Nearly a year here.
The spies return; the people refuse to go up. Thirty-eight years of wandering follow.
Aaron dies and is buried on the mountain.
Balaam blesses Israel; Moses delivers Deuteronomy and dies on Nebo.
Josue crosses the Jordan on dry ground; the walls fall.

journeys.name: Exile and return
journeys.blurb: Jerusalem to Babylon in chains, and back by decree of a Persian king.

stops.t: Nabuchodonosor burns the Temple and carries the people away (586 BC).
King Sedecias sees his sons killed, then is blinded and taken in chains.
'Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept.' Ezechiel and Daniel in exile.
Esther at the Persian court; Nehemias the cupbearer hears of Jerusalem's ruin.
Cyrus's decree (538 BC): the exiles may go home and rebuild.
The altar rebuilt, the second Temple dedicated (515 BC), the walls raised by Nehemias, the Law read by Esdras.

journeys.name: The life of Jesus
journeys.blurb: Bethlehem to Egypt to Nazareth; Galilee to Jerusalem.

stops.t: The Annunciation: Gabriel comes to Mary.
Mary visits Elizabeth; the Magnificat.
The birth; shepherds and Magi.
Presented in the Temple; Simeon's Nunc dimittis.
The flight from Herod.
Thirty hidden years; 'he was subject to them'.
Baptised by John; 'This is my beloved Son'.
Forty days; three temptations.
Water into wine — the first sign.
His own town: the paralytic through the roof, Peter's mother-in-law, the bread of life discourse.
The Sermon on the Mount.
'Thou art Christ, the Son of the living God.'
The Transfiguration.
Blind Bartimeus; Zacheus in the sycamore.
Lazarus raised; Mary anoints his feet.
Palm Sunday, the Last Supper, Gethsemani, Golgotha, the empty tomb.
Known in the breaking of the bread.
Breakfast on the shore; 'Feed my sheep'.
The Ascension.

journeys.name: Paul's first journey
journeys.blurb: With Barnabas to Cyprus and the highlands of Galatia.

stops.t: 'Separate me Saul and Barnabas' — the church sends them.
They sail for Cyprus.
Preaching in the synagogues of Cyprus.
The magician Elymas struck blind; the proconsul believes. Saul is now called Paul.
John Mark turns back.
Paul's great synagogue sermon; 'we turn to the Gentiles'.
The city divided; a plot to stone them.
A cripple healed; hailed as Mercury and Jupiter; Paul stoned and left for dead.
Many disciples made; then back through every city to strengthen them.
They report 'how he had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles'.

journeys.name: Paul's second journey
journeys.blurb: Across to Europe: Philippi, Thessalonica, Athens, Corinth.

stops.t: Paul and Barnabas part; Paul takes Silas.
Timothy joins them.
The vision: 'Pass over into Macedonia and help us'.
Lydia baptised; Paul and Silas sing in prison; the jailer converted.
Three sabbaths in the synagogue; a riot; 'these men turn the world upside down'.
They 'searched the scriptures daily'.
The altar 'To the unknown God'; the sermon on the Areopagus.
Eighteen months with Aquila and Priscilla; the first letters (to the Thessalonians) written.
A brief visit; he promises to return.
He greets the church and goes down to Antioch.

journeys.name: Paul's third journey
journeys.blurb: Three years in Ephesus, then a farewell tour toward Jerusalem.

stops.t: Through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening the disciples.
The disciples of John baptised; the lecture-hall of Tyrannus; books of magic burned; the riot of the silversmiths. Letters to Corinth and Galatia.
Through Macedonia; 2 Corinthians written.
Three months; the Letter to the Romans written here.
Eutychus falls from the window during a long sermon and is raised.
Farewell to the elders of Ephesus: 'I know that you all shall see my face no more'.
Disciples warn him not to go up to Jerusalem.
Agabus binds his own hands with Paul's girdle.
Seized in the Temple; rescued by Roman soldiers; his defence on the stairs.

journeys.name: Paul's voyage to Rome
journeys.blurb: A prisoner's voyage: storm, shipwreck on Malta, and the Appian Way.

stops.t: Two years in custody; before Felix, Festus and Agrippa. 'I appeal to Caesar.'
The centurion Julius lets him visit friends.
Transferred to an Alexandrian grain ship.
Paul warns against sailing on; the captain sails anyway.
Fourteen days driven by the storm Euroaquilo; 'there shall be no loss of any man's life'.
Shipwreck; the viper on Paul's hand; three months on the island.
Three days in Sicily.
Landfall in Italy; brethren found.
Two years under house arrest, 'preaching the kingdom of God... without prohibition'. Tradition: martyred under Nero on the Ostian Way.
